response: {"hypotheses":[{"title":"Bounded Per-Module Coverage Ledger","claim":"Appending exactly this instruction — 'Before editing, spend at most 90 seconds making a compact per-module ledger of every distinct required behavior and error condition; implement against it, and before finishing mark each item with either a code location or one executed check, fixing any unmarked item first.' — will increase the proportion of timed multi-module trials that pass all held-out tests versus no appended instruction, without increasing deadline misses.","rationale":"Dispersed specifications overload working memory and make completion of one module erase less salient requirements from another. A short external ledger converts those requirements into persistent retrieval cues; the evidence-or-check mark makes omissions observable before completion. The 90-second cap directly bounds front-loaded overhead, while code-location evidence permits cheap verification when executing a separate test would be wasteful.","assumptions":["Baseline failures include omitted stated behaviors across modules","A compact ledger can be created within 90 seconds","The agent treats missing evidence as a repair signal rather than fabricating evidence","The intervention leaves enough execution time for implementation"],"risks":["Ledger construction can consume scarce time and raise deadline failures","The agent may copy requirements mechanically without prioritizing difficult ones","Code-location marks can be superficial or incorrect","On tasks dominated by algorithmic difficulty rather than omission, the ledger adds overhead without benefit"]}]}
